ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Gathering of the Whakapapa / Tā Moko

fullPassage:
Gathering of the Whakapapa

The phone rang, and it was my dad calling from my hometown, Waituhi.
"Can you take a week off?" he asked. "Your Nani Tama wants you here."
"But Dad!" I answered. "My boss won't let me take any more time off."
The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say faintly, "I need your help, Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the whakapapa. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have much time."
I just knew I had no choice. "All right, Nani," I replied with a sigh. "I'll come."

For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. In only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina.
Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more. The village went quiet and listened to his chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, searching back across the centuries. Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant. The village waited in worried silence until the next name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to drive him to Murupara to finish his work.

When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was.
"Look, Nani," I said. "I'm not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!"
Nani looked at me in anger.
"You want me to die here in this room? Looking at these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?"
The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car, and we set off with Auntie.

We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky.

Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called Murupara.
"Where do we go now?" I asked Nani.
He did not reply, but he was searching inside himself, staring at the small houses. Then, at a street corner, he told us to turn. After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry."

Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct.
Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment of silence, the old man whispered to Nani, "Goodbye, friend." Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.

It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us.
Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired.
He sighed. "At last, I may go now."
Then, he closed his eyes.
"No, Dad!" Auntie Hiraina cried.
The sun burst across the hills.

Deep Learning: Tā Moko: A Record of an Individual's Path

Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage for the next generation.

questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy ①<u>writing</u> down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. But then came the night of the fire, ②<u>which</u> ran through the house and destroyed our past. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter. ③<u>Trying</u> to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again. He chanted the names of the ancestors, ④<u>joined</u> the past to the present once more.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 조상의 이름을 외우며 과거를 현재에 다시 연결하면서(joining).
det.analysis: ✅ ④ joined → joining: 'chanted ~, joining ~'에서 동시동작 분사구문. 과거형 joined가 아닌 현재분사 joining이 필요. ❌ ① writing: 'be busy + -ing' 적절. ❌ ② which: 계속적 관계대명사 적절. ❌ ③ Trying: 분사구문(이유) 적절.
det.tip: 분사구문(동시동작): S + V ~, V-ing ~. chanted ~, joining ~ (외우며, 연결하면서).

questions.passage: Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult ①<u>to remember</u>. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant. The village waited in worried silence ②<u>until</u> the next name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama almost two years ③<u>gathering</u> most of the whakapapa. Now, he wanted me ④<u>to drive</u> him to Murupara to finish his work.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 나니 타마가 대부분의 족보를 모으는 데 거의 2년이 걸렸다(to gather).
det.analysis: ✅ ③ gathering → to gather: 'It takes + 시간 + to V' 가주어 구문에서 to부정사 필요. ❌ ① to remember: 'difficult to V(~하기 어려운)' 적절. ❌ ② until: '~까지' 시간 접속사 적절. ❌ ④ to drive: 'wanted me to drive(내게 운전해 달라고 원했다)' 적절.
det.tip: It takes + 시간 + to V = ~하는 데 (시간)이 걸리다. want + O + to V.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, ①<u>which</u> has been a culturally significant practice for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also ②<u>symbolic</u> of an individual's journey. Each curved line represents a person's whakapapa and personal ③<u>accomplishment</u>. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still ④<u>practiced</u> today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their traditions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 각 곡선은 한 사람의 족보와 개인적 업적들(accomplishments)을 나타낸다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ accomplishment → accomplishments: 원문은 'personal accomplishments'(복수). 여러 업적을 나타내므로 복수형이 필요. whakapapa, social positions와 병렬. ❌ ① which: 선행사 tattooing을 수식하는 계속적 관계대명사 적절. ❌ ② symbolic: 'not only A but also B' 병렬 구조에서 형용사 적절. ❌ ④ practiced: 수동태 'is practiced by' 적절.
det.tip: 병렬 구조에서 수 일치: positions(복수)와 accomplishments(복수) 병렬.

questions.passage: When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was. Nani looked at me in ①<u>anger</u>. "You want me to die here in this room?" The old man held on ②<u>tightly</u> to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, ③<u>painless</u> step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but ④<u>carry</u> him to the car.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 모든 느리고 고통스러운(painful) 걸음이 그를 아프게 했다. painless(고통 없는)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ③painless(고통 없는): 원문은 painful(고통스러운). 한 걸음마다 아팠다(hurt him)는 맥락과 정반대. ❌ ①anger(분노): 손자의 거절에 화가 난 맥락 적절. ❌ ②tightly(꽉): 침대에 꽉 붙잡았다는 맥락 적절. ❌ ④carry(나르다): 걷지 못해 안아서 옮긴 맥락 적절.
det.tip: painful(고통스러운) ↔ painless(고통 없는). 접미사 -less = ~없는. -ful = ~가 있는.

questions.passage: It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were ①<u>waiting</u> for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and ②<u>offered</u> it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had ③<u>abandoned</u> our past for us. Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew ④<u>tired</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 할아버지가 우리의 과거를 구해주셨기(saved) 때문에 마음이 벅찼다. abandoned(포기했다)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ③abandoned(포기했다): 원문은 saved(구했다). 족보를 완성해 과거를 구한 것이지 포기한 것이 아님. ❌ ①waiting(기다리고 있는): 원문 그대로. ❌ ②offered(바쳤다): 원문 그대로. ❌ ④tired(지친): 미소가 지쳐갔다는 원문 그대로.
det.tip: save(구하다) ↔ abandon(포기하다). Our hearts were full = 마음이 벅찼다.

questions.passage: Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina. Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more. The village went quiet and __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 마을은 조용해졌고 그의 구송에 귀를 기울였다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②listened to his chanting: 원문 표현. 마을이 조용해진 이유는 경청하기 위해서. ❌ ①joined in the chanting: 마을 사람들이 함께 외웠다는 내용 없음. ❌ ③celebrated: 아직 완성 전이므로 축하 부적절. ❌ ④ignored: 무시가 아니라 경청.
det.tip: go quiet = 조용해지다. listen to = ~에 귀 기울이다.

questions.passage: After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry." All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were __________ to see if the work was correct.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: looking over the shoulders of the two old men

det.korean: 과거의 사람들이 두 노인의 어깨 너머로 보고 있는 것 같았다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①looking over the shoulders of the two old men: 원문 표현. 조상들이 작업을 지켜보는 듯한 신비로운 느낌. ❌ ②standing outside: 방 안에 있는 느낌이라고 했으므로 부적절. ❌ ③writing down: 기록은 두 노인이 하는 것. ❌ ④arguing: 다투는 느낌이 아니라 지켜보는 느낌.
det.tip: look over one's shoulder = 어깨 너머로 보다. as if = 마치 ~인 것처럼.

questions.passage: The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. In only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina. Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 족보는 원래 이모의 집에 보관되어 있었다.
화재 후 나니 타마는 아들의 집으로 갔다.
나니 타마는 화재 후 떨리는 손으로 족보를 다시 쓰기 시작했다.

det.korean: 나니 타마는 화재 후 떨리는 손으로 족보를 다시 쓰기 시작했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④: 'began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands' 일치. ❌ ①: 족보는 '그의 오래된 집(his old house)'에 있었지 이모 집이 아님. ❌ ②: '딸(daughter, Auntie Hiraina)' 집으로 감. ❌ ③: 'In only one night'으로 하루 밤.
det.tip: shaky: 떨리는. in despair: 절망 속에. daughter ≠ son.

questions.passage: We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky. Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called Murupara.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 나니가 이모에게 노래를 가르쳐 준 것이지, 이모가 나니에게 가르친 것이 아니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 원문은 'a song that he had taught Auntie'로 나니가 이모에게 가르침. 방향이 뒤바뀜. ❌ ①: 'mostly in silence' 일치. ❌ ③: 'Just before noon' 일치. ❌ ④: 'They sang together' 일치.
det.tip: 주어-목적어 관계 주의: he(Nani) had taught Auntie = 나니가 이모에게 가르침.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey. Each curved line and pattern represents a person's whakapapa, social positions, and personal accomplishments. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 타 모코는 순수하게 장식적인 목적만 가진다.
마오리족 여성은 얼굴 전체에 타 모코를 새긴다.
마오리족은 십대부터 타 모코를 새기기 시작한다.
타 모코의 무늬는 모든 사람에게 동일하다.

det.korean: 마오리족은 십대부터 타 모코를 새기기 시작한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 'start getting these designs in their teenage years' 일치. ❌ ①: 'not only decorative but also symbolic'이므로 장식만은 아님. ❌ ②: 여성은 'lips and chins'이지 얼굴 전체가 아님. ❌ ④: 'no two designs look the same'이므로 모두 다름.
det.tip: teenage years: 십대. not only A but also B: A뿐만 아니라 B도.

questions.passage: The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say faintly, "I need your help, Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the whakapapa." For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which destroyed our past. It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa. Finally, after traveling to Murupara, the work was done. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us.
questions.stem: 위 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: The Night of the Terrible Fire
How the Maori Village Was Built
Saving the Past: A Grandfather's Mission

det.korean: 이 글의 제목은 과거를 구하다: 할아버지의 사명이 가장 적절하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④: 화재로 잃은 족보를 복원하는 할아버지의 여정이 핵심. ❌ ①: 가족 여행이 아니라 사명을 위한 여정. ❌ ②: 화재는 배경일 뿐 주제가 아님. ❌ ③: 마을 건설과 무관.
det.tip: mission: 사명, 임무. save the past: 과거를 구하다.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern represents a person's whakapapa, social positions, and personal accomplishments. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage for the next generation.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 개인의 정체성과 역사를 담은 마오리 전통 문신의 의미
현대 사회에서 전통 문신이 사라지는 이유

det.korean: 이 글의 주제는 개인의 정체성과 역사를 담은 마오리 전통 문신의 의미이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 장식+상징(족보, 지위, 업적)+통과 의례+보존 노력까지 핵심 내용 포괄. ❌ ①: 기술 발전 과정은 다루지 않음. ❌ ③: less common이지만 still practiced이므로 사라지는 것이 아님. ❌ ④: 의학적 이유 언급 없음.
det.tip: identity: 정체성. symbolic: 상징적인. rite of passage: 통과 의례.

questions.passage: Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired. He sighed. <u>"At last, I may go now."</u> Then, he closed his eyes. "No, Dad!" Auntie Hiraina cried. The sun burst across the hills.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 "At last, I may go now."가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 이제 집으로 돌아가서 쉴 수 있다.
드디어 다음 여행을 떠날 수 있다.
족보를 완성했으니 이제 편히 눈을 감을 수 있다.
이제 무루파라로 다시 갈 수 있다.

det.korean: "드디어 이제 갈 수 있다" = 족보를 완성했으니 편히 눈을 감을 수 있다(죽음의 완곡 표현).
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 'go'는 죽음의 완곡한 표현. 직후 'closed his eyes', 이모의 울부짖음, 해돋이가 이를 확인. ❌ ①: 단순히 집에 가는 것이 아님. ❌ ②: 여행이 아니라 삶의 마무리. ❌ ④: 무루파라에서 이미 돌아옴.
det.tip: go = 죽음의 완곡 표현(euphemism). 'The sun burst across the hills' = 일출이 할아버지의 영혼을 상징.

questions.passage: He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more. The village went quiet and listened to <u>his</u> chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy. Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant. The village waited in worried silence until the next name burst out of his mouth.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 his가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나니 타마가 조상의 이름을 외우며 족보를 재구성하는 장면.
det.analysis: ✅ ①Nani Tama: 'He chanted'의 주어가 나니 타마이며, 이후 'his voice', 'his chanting' 모두 같은 인물. ❌ ②narrator: 화자는 관찰자. ❌ ③father: 아버지는 전화만 걸었음. ❌ ④old man in Murupara: 아직 무루파라에 가기 전.
det.tip: 대명사 추적: He(Nani) → his chanting → His voice → his mouth. 모두 나니 타마.

questions.passage: After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry." Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table. All through the quiet afternoon, <u>they</u> recalled missing names.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 they가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Nani Tama and the old man in Murupara

det.korean: 나니 타마와 무루파라의 노인이 빠진 이름을 회상했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 'the two old men sitting at the table'이 바로 나니 타마와 무루파라의 노인. 'they recalled missing names'의 주어. ❌ ①: 화자와 이모는 지켜보는 입장. ❌ ②: 마을 사람들은 고향에 남아 있음. ❌ ④: 과거의 조상들은 실제로 참여하지 않음.
det.tip: they = the two old men = Nani Tama + the old man in Murupara. recall: 회상하다.

questions.passage: It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

나니 타마가 족보를 들어 올려 마을에 바치자, 할아버지가 우리의 과거를 구해주셨기 때문에 우리의 가슴이 __________.

det.korean: 우리의 가슴이 가득 찼다(full).
det.analysis: ✅ full: 원문 'Our hearts were full'에서 직접 찾을 수 있음.
det.tip: Our hearts were full = 우리의 마음이 벅찼다/가득 찼다.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also __________ (symbol) of an individual's journey from their past to their present.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 장식적일 뿐만 아니라 개인의 여정을 상징하는(symbolic) 것이기도 하다.
det.analysis: ✅ symbolic: 'not only decorative(형용사) but also symbolic(형용사)' 병렬. symbol(명사) → symbolic(형용사).
det.tip: symbol(명사: 상징) → symbolic(형용사: 상징적인). 병렬 구조: not only A but also B에서 A, B 동일 품사.

questions.passage: It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to drive him to Murupara to finish his work. When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was. __________.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 빈칸을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[ I / not / could / but / help / carry / him / to / the / car ]
questions.wa: I could not help but carry him to the car
accept: I could not help but carry him to the car
i could not help but carry him to the car
I could not help but carry him to the car.

det.korean: 나는 그를 차까지 데려다 드릴 수밖에 없었다.
det.analysis: ✅ I could not help but carry him to the car: 'could not help but + 동사원형' 구문.
det.tip: cannot help but V = ~하지 않을 수 없다. = cannot help V-ing.

questions.passage: The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say faintly, "I need your help, Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the whakapapa. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have much time."
questions.stem:
위 글을 참고하여 다음 빈칸을 영어로 완성하시오.

할아버지는 손자에게 족보를 완성하기 위해 무루파라까지 운전해 달라고 부탁했다. 서두르라고 하셨는데, 시간이 많지 않을 수도 있기 때문이었다.

His grandfather asked him to __________ him to Murupara.

det.korean: 할아버지는 손자에게 무루파라까지 운전해(drive) 달라고 부탁했다.
det.analysis: ✅ drive: 원문 'Drive me there'에서 직접 확인. 'asked him to drive'는 'wanted me to drive'의 패러프레이징.
det.tip: ask + O + to V = O에게 V해 달라고 부탁하다. drive: 운전하다, 태워다 주다.

questions.passage: Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye. It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us.
questions.stem:
위 글을 참고하여 다음 빈칸을 영어로 완성하시오.

두 노인은 울면서 작별 인사를 하기 위해 코를 맞댔다. 이모 집에 돌아오니 마을 사람들이 우리를 기다리고 있었다.

They pressed their __________ together to say goodbye.

det.korean: 그들은 작별 인사를 하기 위해 코(noses)를 맞댔다.
det.analysis: ✅ noses: 원문 'pressed their noses together'. 마오리식 전통 인사(hongi).
det.tip: press noses together = 코를 맞대다 (마오리 전통 인사 hongi). nose의 복수형: noses.
